key_insight: CAVQS reduces two-qubit gate counts by optimizing across circuit-block boundaries and exploiting permitted terminal measurements with classical feedforward.
engineering_relevance: Lower CNOT costs could ease hardware execution, while dynamic implementations require measurement and feedforward support.
method: Use QR decomposition to redistribute unitary factors across overlapping blocks while preserving the overall transformation.
Resynthesize context-adjusted blocks to enable cross-block gate reductions.
For eligible terminal-measurement blocks, combine CNOT-budgeted search with analytic branch unitaries to minimize expected CNOT cost without ancillas.
evidence_signal: On common successful random-circuit instances, mean two-qubit gate reductions range from 2.05% to 74.64% across three baselines; reported reductions on 4–6-qubit algorithm benchmarks range from 20.65% to 71.88%.
watch_item: Dynamic reconstruction applies only where terminal measurements are permitted, and gate-count savings alone do not establish hardware-level speed or fidelity gains.
paper_title: CAVQS: Context-Aware Variational Quantum Circuit Synthesis via Unitary Redistribution and Dynamic Reconstruction
